candidate_law.name: constant-intake security throughput and reserve ceiling
candidate_law.setup: A locality receives the same recruit intake N at the start of every update interval Delta. Training rate tau and reserve attrition mu are constant. Ignore deployment cost/target constraints while deriving the stock-flow ceiling.
candidate_law.zero_attrition_case: If b=1, reserve changes by N-Y per steady-state interval; Y=N is the non-drifting throughput boundary.

predictions: For tau>0 and constant intake, graduation throughput converges monotonically from below to N regardless of tau.
Higher tau shortens the time required to reach any fixed fraction of steady graduation but does not raise D_star.
The steady trainee stock G_star decreases as training becomes faster.
With reserve attrition and no other inflow, constant deployment Y>b*N eventually depletes reserve, whereas Y<=b*N is sustainable after the training transient given sufficient initial reserve.
The production transition helpers reproduce the closed-form recurrence to floating-point tolerance.
production_equivalence_required: Iterating security_training_transition with recurring N must match the closed-form G_m and D_m recurrence.
Iterating security_reserve_after_attrition and a constant deployment subtraction must match the closed-form reserve recurrence.
The long-run graduation limit must be independent of tau for tau>0.
The sustainable deployment boundary must match b*N in the production arithmetic.
claim_boundary: SL12 is an exact theorem of Pineland's synthetic training/reserve recurrence. It does not estimate real recruiting, training, attrition, or deployment throughput.
